    Lemma 4.13: weights on L are ratios of object values #

    lem:scalar-object-values. For the deck grading of a scalar mesh category with at most one arrow between two vertices, a weight d on L gives the automorphism Φ of the cover (ScalarAutomorphism.lean). "The endpoints of an arrow differ in height by one, so the entire morphism space between them is spanned by the arrow. Thus Φ(a) = w(a) a for some w(a) ∈ k*" (wArr). "Comparing coefficients gives w(σa) w(a) = ν_X" (mesh_compat). "Assign ν_X to t_X. These weights respect the triangles of K̃. Since this complex is simply connected, multiplying along walks gives object values ζ_X" (ζ, ζ_arrow). "Conjugation by these values fixes every arrow and hence every morphism, so Φ multiplies each morphism X̃ → Ỹ by ζ_Ỹ / ζ_X̃" (Φ_eq_ratio), and on L this gives d(x, y) = ζ_y / ζ_x (weight_eq_ratio).

    References #

    • Multiplicative bases and deformations of representation-finite algebras, https://github.com/haruhisa-enomoto/multiplicative-bases-deformations. Numbered statements cited here refer to it.
